subject: Follow-up: Redwood pricing & token economics — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Torres <dtorres@finex.com>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finex.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood pricing & token economics — next steps

Hi Danielle & Marcus,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the clear context on your primary use cases (support summarization + search re-ranking) and the projected monthly volume. To recap the items we discussed and the asks I promised: 

- Current expected steady-state volume: ~30M tokens/month (peaks ~75M in campaign months) — see attached Finex-usage-report.csv that Marcus shared.
- Target unit economics: you mentioned an internal goal of ~$700–$900 per 1M tokens (all-in, including reserve capacity/backstop) to make this work for the churn model.
- Primary constraints: finance needs predictable unit pricing and clear forecast to sign off; security review is already in progress (SOC2 docs shared earlier).

Next steps I propose: 
1) Confirm the economic buyer & budget owner for the project so we can tailor the pricing/commit: who owns sign-off in your finance org (economic buyer) vs who will manage the purchase order / budget (budget owner)?
2) I will share an updated pricing proposal (including a 12-month reserved capacity discount + burst pricing) by Monday that targets the $/1M token range we discussed.
3) If relevant, we can run a 30-day pilot on a small reserved pool to validate latency & token burn trends before a full commit.

Please confirm the names/roles for the economic buyer and budget owner so I can align legal/procurement/finance in our next iteration.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Finex-usage-report.csv (summary)
From: Danielle Torres <dtorres@finex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finex.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood pricing & token economics — next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and for pulling this together. Clear and accurate. A couple of quick clarifications from our side: 

- Economic buyer: I will be the economic buyer for strategy sign-off (I own the product budget and roadmap).
- Budget owner / finance sign-off: Marcus (cc'd) is our VP Finance and will own the PO + final sign-off on spend.

On the target unit economics: our leadership has set a goal of around $750/1M tokens as the threshold to move forward at scale. If you can get close to that with a reasonable reserved commitment and transparent overage pricing, we should be in good shape.

Can you include a short worked example in the proposal (3 scenarios: baseline 30M, scaled 75M, and pilot 10M) that shows monthly spend and effective $/1M for each? That will help me make the case.

Thanks — Danielle
Danielle Torres
Head of Product 
Finex (dtorres@finex.com)
From: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Danielle Torres <dtorres@finex.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood pricing & token economics — next steps

Marissa — added for clarity: I will review the pricing with finance operations and confirm procurement timelines. A couple of asks from finance: 

- Please include a clear monthly invoicing cadence and what reserve/commit looks like on the invoice.
- Clarify breakpoints for discounted tiers and how overages are calculated (flat $/1M vs sliding tiers).
- Procurement timeline: assuming numbers look good, we typically need ~3 weeks for PO and ~2 weeks for Legal to turn paperwork for a mid-market vendor.

If you can get the $/1M to sit at ~$750 on the mid-case (30M) with improved scale to ~$650 on 75M, we are in a great position to propose the PO.

Thanks,
Marcus
VP Finance | Finex
marcus.lee@finex.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Torres <dtorres@finex.com>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Follow-up: Redwood pricing & token economics — next steps

Hi Danielle & Marcus — looping in Aditya from Pricing/RevOps (that's me). Per Marissa's note and your asks, attached is an updated proposal that includes: 

- Three worked scenarios (pilot 10M, baseline 30M, scaled 75M) with monthly spend and effective $/1M tokens.
- A 12-month reserved plan that targets ~$740/1M at 30M with burst pricing that reduces to ~$640/1M at 75M. 
- Clear invoice cadence (monthly) and a sample invoice line items table.
- Breakpoints and overage calculation (overage billed at a pre-agreed $/1M or sliding tiers depending on commitment).

Next suggested steps: 
1) Danielle confirms this aligns with the $750 target — if so, Marcus: can you validate procurement timeline and any additional PO requirements?
2) If approved, we'll generate a DocuSign-ready SOW + pricing addendum and share it via the link below so your legal team can review.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/FINEX-Redwood-Proposal
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-2026-1472

I'll attach the PDF proposal now (Redwood-pricing-proposal-v2.pdf). Happy to jump on a short sync with finance next week if useful.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood-pricing-proposal-v2.pdf
